facts.statement: Passing on the right is permitted on a one-way road marked with at least two lanes traveling in the same direction.
Do not use the shoulder to pass except for an emergency or instructions from traffic authorities.
Check ahead and behind and signal before passing on the right.
Following distance must be reasonable for weather, roadway and traffic conditions.
Leave enough following space to stop or turn if the vehicle ahead stops abruptly.
The handbook uses a two-second following interval for ideal conditions.
The handbook uses a four-second following interval when conditions are adverse.
Increase the following gap behind vehicles likely to stop frequently or turn abruptly.
Poor weather calls for an even greater following gap.
Following too closely limits the view of traffic and road conditions ahead.
At a stop sign, stop at the marked stop line when one is present.
At a stop sign with no stop line, stop before the near-side crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop nearest the intersecting roadway.
Stop when leaving an alley, private drive or building in a residential or business area.
Stop when a school crossing guard holds the official flag in the stop position.
Stop when directed by a railroad-crossing flagger or control device.
Stop when a construction flagger directs you to do so.
Stop whenever a police officer directs you to stop.
For an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing red lights or a siren, pull right and stop clear of intersections.
A flashing red traffic light requires a complete stop.
Unless on the opposing roadway of a divided highway, a driver meeting or overtaking a school, church or day-care bus stopped to load or unload children must stop.
After stopping for a school, church or day-care bus loading or unloading children, remain stopped until its stop signal retracts and red lights turn off.
Traffic on the opposing roadway of a divided highway need not stop for a school bus loading or unloading children.
Yield to a vehicle that has already entered the intersection from another road.
When vehicles enter an intersection from different roadways at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.
At a stop-controlled entrance to a through road, stop and enter only without interfering with traffic.
An emergency vehicle using a forward red light or a siren or bell has priority.
For an emergency vehicle using a forward red light, siren or bell, pull right and remain stopped until it has passed.
Do not follow an emergency vehicle responding with warning signals.

When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights from behind on a road with at least two lanes in each direction, cautiously move out of its adjacent lane if a lane change is possible.
If a lane change is impossible when approaching from behind a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights on a road with at least two lanes each way, slow down and proceed cautiously.
Yield to construction workers and vehicles actively working on the road.
Move to a lane away from a construction vehicle working on the roadway.
A left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic.
When a left-turning vehicle and a straight-moving vehicle enter together, the straight-moving vehicle has priority.
A vehicle entering from a private drive or side road yields to traffic on the public roadway.
Before crossing the sidewalk from an alley, driveway or building in a business or residential district, stop and then yield.
At a yield sign, stop only when needed to avoid interfering with priority traffic or pedestrians.
Do not enter an intersection, crosswalk or railroad crossing without space beyond it for your vehicle.
A green signal does not permit entering an intersection that lacks room beyond it.
Parking inside an intersection is prohibited.
Parking in an intersection crosswalk is prohibited.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Do not park with the vehicle more than 12 inches from the curb.
Parking in front of a driveway is prohibited.
Parking on a highway bridge or elevated structure is prohibited.
Parking inside a tunnel is prohibited.
Do not park where official signs prohibit parking.
Double parking along the curb or roadside is prohibited.
Do not park on a narrow road where the vehicle would obstruct ordinary traffic.
Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited.
Do not park within the 30-foot approach to a roadside signal, stop sign or flashing beacon.
Do not park between a safety zone and the nearby curb.
Do not park within 30 feet of the curb points opposite the ends of a safety zone.
Keep parked vehicles at least 50 feet from the nearest railroad-crossing rail.
Do not park within 20 feet of a fire-station driveway entrance.
On the opposite side of a fire-station entrance, the handbook prohibits parking within 75 feet.
Do not park beside or opposite roadwork or another obstruction when doing so would block traffic.
The handbook lists designated disability-parking spaces among restricted parking locations.
Kansas prohibits composing, sending or reading written electronic communication while driving.
The written-communication restriction includes text messages and email.
The handbook excludes GPS use and weather reports from its written-communication prohibition.
Talking or dialing on a cell phone is not specifically prohibited by the general rule described in this section.
A distracting activity remains dangerous even when it is not specifically prohibited.
Move out of an aggressive driver's way.
Do not provoke an aggressive driver by accelerating or defending your place in traffic.
Avoid eye contact that could further anger an aggressive driver.
Ignore hostile gestures or insults without responding in kind.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Without a stop line, stop before the near-side crosswalk, or nearest the intersecting roadway if no crosswalk exists.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: At a stop sign with no stop line, stop before the near-side crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop nearest the intersecting roadway.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone fact drops the stop-sign condition and can imply stopping at every unmarked intersection.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Drivers meeting or overtaking a school, church or day-care bus stopped for children must stop.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Unless on the opposing roadway of a divided highway, a driver meeting or overtaking a school, church or day-care bus stopped to load or unload children must stop.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone mandatory-stop statement omits the opposing-roadway divided-highway exception.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Remain stopped for a children's bus until its stop signal retracts and its red lights go out.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: After stopping for a school, church or day-care bus loading or unloading children, remain stopped until its stop signal retracts and red lights turn off.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Children's bus is broader and less precise than the three named categories.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Traffic on the opposing roadway of a divided highway need not stop for the bus.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Traffic on the opposing roadway of a divided highway need not stop for a school bus loading or unloading children.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The bus has no self-contained antecedent and omits the source's school-bus category.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: If vehicles arrive from different roads at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the right-hand driver.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: When vehicles enter an intersection from different roadways at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Arrive is substituted for the source's enter trigger, and intersection is omitted.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Stay stopped to the right until the emergency vehicle passes.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For an emergency vehicle using a forward red light, siren or bell, pull right and remain stopped until it has passed.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone instruction loses the warning-signal activation condition.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle from behind on a road with at least two lanes each way, cautiously move out of the adjacent lane.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights from behind on a road with at least two lanes in each direction, cautiously move out of its adjacent lane if a lane change is possible.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The flashing warning lights are omitted, and the unavailable-lane-change exception is not self-contained.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: If changing lanes beside a stopped emergency vehicle is impossible, slow down and proceed cautiously.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: If a lane change is impossible when approaching from behind a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights on a road with at least two lanes each way, slow down and proceed cautiously.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone fallback loses the rear approach, flashing-warning-light and road-lane conditions.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Before crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway in a business or residential district, stop and then yield.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Before crossing the sidewalk from an alley, driveway or building in a business or residential district, stop and then yield.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The pre-sidewalk stop/yield procedure also covers emergence from a building. R13 covers a building exit generally, but R37's precise sidewalk timing omits that category.
